definition: Nocturnal myoclonus refers to involuntary, brief shock-like muscle jerks during the night. These contractions vary in timing and strength and are followed by relaxation.

provenance.scope: Source record D009207; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports involuntary, shock-like contractions that are irregular in rhythm and amplitude and are followed by relaxation, but it does not explicitly support the added claim that they occur “during the night.”
The definition is a bit more interpretive than the source wording; the packet describes contractions of a muscle or group of muscles and does not specifically say “muscle jerks.”
The packet excerpt does not explicitly state that the shock-like contractions occur “during the night,” even though it discusses “NOCTURNAL MYOCLONUS SYNDROME.”
The definition includes “brief” jerks, but the packet does not describe them as brief.
The packet describes irregular rhythm and amplitude, but does not explicitly frame this as “vary in timing,” so that phrasing is not directly supported.
